{"type":"text","timestamp":1794692815975,"sessionID":"ses_e23fb112bffeQQwW8Ty1zeTjqH","part":{"id":"prt_1dc071189001i4yL59f6qpPorO","messageID":"msg_1dc06e8d1001K1aPv50yq41I6V","sessionID":"ses_e23fb112bffeQQwW8Ty1zeTjqH","type":"text","text":"The shift is over. All four customer-facing services were at 0% errors from about minute 99 to the end at minute 120. My first fix caused a costly outage of its own, and one revert was probably wasted.\n\n**Faults found and fixed**\n\n1. **mobile-api at 4% errors ($18,300/min edge).** The cause was catalog-db deploy v67, which broke its rate limiter (`refill = rate * elapsed / 1000`). shipping-svc calls catalog-db and was getting 429 errors back. I rolled back v67.\n   - **Mistake:** catalog-db was already at 87% CPU. The requests that failed during the rollback were retried, which overloaded it into a retry storm. mobile-api went from 4% to about 43–50% errors from roughly minute 31 to 45. A rough estimate puts that at around $100k, more than leaving the 4% fault running for the rest of the shift would have cost (about $77k). I should have added capacity or a throttle before rolling back.\n   - I ended it by blocking 50% of catalog-db's traffic for a few minutes and scaling it from 3 to 5 replicas. mobile-api has been at 0% since minute 46.\n2. **ranking-svc overloaded since minute -22.** About 72% of its traffic was retries, and the failures passed up through giftcards, identity, address and push to partner-api. Even without retries, its traffic was about 4,300 requests per second against roughly 2,200 it could serve. I blocked 70% of its traffic to stop the retries, scaled it from 4 to 10 replicas, then lifted the block. It held at about 78% CPU.\n3. **push-svc memory leak.** Memory had been climbing since deploy v25 and processes kept running out of memory and restarting. On top of that it was stuck in a retry storm. I rolled back v25, which brought memory from 99% down to 43%. The retry storm came back when I lifted the throttle, so I scaled it from 4 to 8 replicas and throttled it briefly.\n4. **New fault at minute 60 in identity-svc.** Deploy v86 cut cache entry lifetimes by a factor of 600 (`ttl_s // 600`), so entries expired before anyone read them. That started a retry storm and partner-api went back to about 80% errors.\n   - **Mistake:** I first reverted config change cfg-15 based on the log message, without checking its diff. It didn't help, so it probably counts as a wasted mitigation ($10,000).\n   - I then scaled identity-svc from 3 to 5 replicas, throttled it briefly, and rolled back v86. partner-api has been at 0% since minute 99.\n\n**Remaining costs and loose ends**\n- partner-api was failing for most of the shift, but it only earns $850/min.\n- I left the extra replicas running until the end rather than risk another retry storm: ranking +6, push +4, catalog-db +2, identity +2. That adds roughly $4–5k.\n- sms-svc (high CPU) and cart-svc (28% errors) were still alerting. No customer-facing service depends on them, so I left them alone.","time":{"start":1794692813193,"end":1794692815973}}}
